chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the beautiful, immoral woman: Is it permissible for a man to enjoy her for a day or more? He said: If she is well-known for adultery, then he should not enjoy her, nor marry her.

key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعَ: To enjoy (specifically referring to Mut'a or temporary marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Mut'a with a promiscuous woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the condition of chastity (al-Zawja al-Zakia) required for Mut'a by excluding women 'known for adultery' (mashhura bi-zin), a criterion often interpreted by Shia jurists as requiring public reputation rather than absolute virginity. This ruling underscores the principle that temporary marriage is not merely a license for casual sex but requires a baseline of sexual propriety, distinguishing it from permanent marriage where broader criteria may apply.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the woman, the beautiful, the immoral. Is it allowed for the man that he does Mut’a with her for a day, or more?’ So heasws said: ‘If it was such that she was well known with the adultery, so he cannot do Mut’a with her, nor sleep with her’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn af-Fudayl who has said the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who was beautiful but was involved in indecent acts if it was permissible to form al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) with her for a day or more. He (the Imam) said, ’If she is known as a fornicator then al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) is not proper with her as well as marriage.’”
